evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.13: holusculīs nōs solēs pāscere
terms.comment: First of animals, which it also takes out to graze; of people too, as when Cicero teases Atticus for always feeding him vegetables. The passive pāscor is to feed, to graze.
Rare. Suetonius’s Tiberius fed his pet snake by hand; with people as object the verb is late (Vulgate).

evidence: Tac. Germ. 20.1: sua quemque māter ūberibus alit
terms.comment: Feeding that brings up: a mother nursing her baby.

terms.gloss: suckle, nourish, feed, bring up, rear
evidence: Ov. F. 2.415: quōs lupa nūtrit (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 2.4.40: īlignā nūtrītus glande (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: vēlōcēs Spartae catulōs ācremque Molossum pāsce serō pinguī
phrases.english: feed the swift Spartan puppies and the fierce mastiff on rich whey

phrases.latin: Respicite volātilia caelī … et Pater vester caelestis pāscit illa.
phrases.english: Look at the birds of the air … and your heavenly Father feeds them.

phrases.latin: hōc pinguem et placitam Pācī nūtrītor olīvam
phrases.english: in this way rear the rich olive that Peace loves
Let’s throw the ducks some breadcrumbs.

phrases.latin: melle sopōrātam et medicātīs frūgibus offam objicit
phrases.english: she throws him a cake made drowsy with honey and drugged grain (the Sibyl feeding Cerberus)
Feed the dog, would you; he’s hungry.

phrases.latin: Cibātus canis propior hominis quam ovis. Pāscitur enim edūliīs et ossibus, nōn herbīs aut fronde.
phrases.english: A dog’s food is nearer a man’s than a sheep’s: he is fed on scraps of food and bones, not on grass or leaves.

phrases.latin: Cibāria gallīnīs praebentur optima pīnsitum hordeum et vicia
phrases.english: The best feed to give hens is crushed barley and vetch

sources: Lewis & Short: pasco · Lewis & Short: cibo · Lewis & Short: alo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 166, 314.
